methods.cut: large or jumbo peeled & deveined raw shrimp (16/20 or 21/25 count)
methods.heat: Medium to medium-high heat in a large skillet
methods.time: 1 to 2 minutes per side (approx. 3 to 4 minutes total)
methods.doneness: Flesh turns from translucent gray to pink, pearly, and opaque throughout; curls into a gentle 'C' shape
methods.rest: None; residual pan heat finishes cooking; serve immediately
methods.tips: Sear shrimp in olive oil first to build color before adding butter and garlic so the butter and garlic do not scorch; cook in uncrowded batches so shrimp sear rather than boil in released juices; turn individually with tongs; deglaze with dry white wine or lemon juice to halt browning and create pan sauce.

source.name: Garlic Prawns (Shrimp) - RecipeTin Eats & The Best Shrimp Scampi - Swanky Recipes
source.location: Skillet browning technique and garlic butter timing

methods.cut: jumbo or large raw shrimp (peeled, deveined, tail-on, e.g. U-8 or 16/20)
methods.time: 5 to 7 minutes at 400°F (or 7 minutes at 425°F for U-8 colossal shrimp)
methods.doneness: Shrimp turn uniformly pink and opaque throughout; springy to the touch
methods.rest: 1 to 2 minutes on the hot baking sheet before serving
methods.tips: Pat shrimp thoroughly dry with paper towels before tossing with olive oil, garlic, and Mediterranean spices; spread across sheet pan in a single uncrowded layer; if serving with roasted vegetables, roast vegetables first on lower rack, then drop oven to 400°F and bake shrimp on top rack during the final 6 minutes.

source.name: Sheet Pan Shrimp | The Mediterranean Dish & How to cook Jumbo Shrimp - Chef Pachi
source.location: Oven baking time, temp, and two-rack vegetable synchronization

methods.cut: large raw shrimp threaded on skewers (peeled, deveined, tail-on)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat on lightly oiled grill pan or outdoor grates
methods.doneness: Pearly white and opaque center with lightly charred grill marks and pink exterior
methods.tips: Marinate briefly (10 minutes) with citrus, oil, and herbs; discard excess marinade before grilling so shrimp char rather than steam; thread skewers through both head and tail ends to prevent spinning on grates.

source.name: Heart Healthy Recipe Guide - HFSA
source.location: Grilled Shrimp Skewers with Mint Salsa Verde, p. 40

methods.cut: 16/20 count raw shrimp (peeled, deveined, room temperature)
methods.heat: Low stovetop heat (bare gentle butter melt)
methods.doneness: Plump, tender, juicy, and opaque throughout without rubberiness
methods.rest: None; serve warm in butter broth with crusty bread
methods.tips: Slowly melt salted butter in a small pot with a splash of water to keep milk solids from breaking down; fully submerge shrimp in the warm butter bath and cook gently.

source.name: Butter Poached Shrimp - SAM THE COOKING GUY

methods.heat: Gentle rolling simmer in broth or sauce
methods.doneness: Pink, opaque, curled into a loose C-shape
methods.tips: Always add raw shrimp during the final 5 to 8 minutes of simmering soups, curries, or gumbos; boiling shrimp early in long-cooked stews overcooks them into tough, rubbery curls.

avoid.warning: Overcooking: shrimp cook in 3 to 6 minutes; leaving them on heat past opacity expels moisture, shrinking them into tough, rubbery, tightly coiled 'O' rings.
Crowding the skillet during pan-searing: overloading the pan drops cooking temperature and causes shrimp to boil in their own rendered moisture rather than searing with color.
Burning minced garlic at high heat: garlic burns easily in high-heat searing; use chopped garlic and add partway through cooking or deglaze with wine to prevent bitter scorched garlic.
Defrosting frozen shrimp in warm or hot water: warm water par-cooks delicate exterior flesh and invites bacterial growth; thaw frozen shrimp in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes.
